newsitem.title: USA: Three Tenors say the fat lady hasn't sung yet.
newsitem.headline: Three Tenors say the fat lady hasn't sung yet.

text.p: The Three Tenors made it clear on Thursday -- the Fat Lady has not yet sung.

After their press representatives said on Wednesday that the three singers -- Luciano Pavarotti, Placido Domingo and Jose Carreras -- would go their separate ways after the Houston concert and never perform together again, the stars said on Thursday that that was not true.

"Why should it be the last concert? We love very much to do these concerts," Pavarotti said in a press conference at the Astrodome, where the March 16 performance will be held. Their world tour began on June 29 in Tokyo.
The three men spoke to reporters via satellite. Carreras and Pavarotti were in Vienna and Domingo in Washington, D.C.
Domingo said the group planned to perform in Paris in 1998 in conjunction with the World Cup, upholding a tradition they began with the World Cup in Italy in 1990 and in Los Angeles in 1994.
"If we are in good health and we are on this planet, we certainly are going to do the 1998 World Cup," he said.
On Wednesday spokeswoman Leslie Sonnenklar had said of the Houston concert: "This is the last and final performance ever. Ever."
